Below is a quick‑look table of the **federal Canadian public holidays that create a natural 3‑day long weekend** in 2023.  
(If you’re in a province that observes additional holidays, you’ll have a few more long weekends—see the “Notes” section.)

| Date | Holiday | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Type |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Monday | **Mon‑Tue** (holiday + weekend) |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | Friday | **Fri‑Sat‑Sun** |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | Monday | **Mon‑Tue** |
| **Jul 3** | Canada Day (observed, because July 1 fell on Saturday) | Monday | **Mon‑Tue** |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | Monday | **Mon‑Tue** |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Monday | **Mon‑Tue** |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas | Monday | **Mon‑Tue** |

### Notes

| Province | Extra Long‑Weekends (2023) |
|----------|---------------------------|
| British Columbia | **Feb 20** (Family Day) – same as above |
| Nova Scotia | **Feb 20** (Family Day) – same as above |
| Newfoundland & Labrador | **Feb 20** (Family Day) – same as above |
| Quebec | **Feb 20** (Family Day) – same as above |
| Yukon | **Feb 20** (Family Day) – same as above |
| Northwest Territories | **Feb 20** (Family Day) – same as above |
| Nunavut | **Feb 20** (Family Day) – same as above |
| **Other provinces** | No additional federal long‑weekends beyond those listed. |

> **Why these dates?**  
> A “long weekend” is usually defined as a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, giving you a three‑day break (Friday–Saturday–Sunday or Saturday–Sunday–Monday). In 2023, the federal holidays that meet that criterion are the ones above.  

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app! If you need province‑specific holidays or want to include “extended” long weekends (e.g., taking a day off on the day before/after a holiday), let me know and I can expand the list.
